meta.title: How A Company Actually Decides Its Own Stock Price On IPO Day
meta.hook: Before a company's stock trades for the first time, its own executives don't set the price. A weeks-long sales pitch does.
meta.description: Going public starts with a roadshow: company executives and underwriting banks pitch large institutional investors over one to two weeks to gauge real demand. That demand determines the final offer price the night before trading begins. Only after that negotiated price is set does the stock open for public trading on an exchange, at whatever price buyers and sellers agree to next. Educational content only, not financial advice.
